newsitem.title: USA: Gardner Denver sees petroleum unit demand rising.
newsitem.headline: Gardner Denver sees petroleum unit demand rising.

text.p: Gardner Denver Machinery Inc said Wednesday that demand for its petroleum products rose significantly in 1996, and the company expects the trend to continue in 1997.

Earlier Gardner Denver, which provides air compressors and blowers for industrial applications and pumps used in oil and gas production, reported fourth quarter earnings of $0.54 a share versus $0.45. For the year, the company earned $1.66 a share compared with $1.19.
The company said excluding acquisitions, demand for its petroleum products increased 37 percent in 1996 versus 1995.

"The company anticipates at least comparable growth in this segment in 1997 and continuing improvements in margins which should result in this segment becoming a significant contributor to the Company's earnings growth during the year," Gardner Denver said in a statement.

Demand for compressed air products should grow slightly more than the expansion of the U.S. economy in 1997, and revenues and earnings should increase as the financial effect of the acquisitions is annualized, the company said.

For the year ended December 31, 1996, revenues in the Compressed Air Products, excluding those from acquisitions in 1996 and casting sales in 1995, rose to $169.3 million from $167.6 million for 1995.
Petroleum products revenues excluding acquisitions in 1996 and drilling components in 1995 were $24.4 million versus $18.8 million.
